title: The Divine Appearance and Sacred Life of Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan
summary: The sacred account of the Hamsa lineage, initiation from Narada, the Sudarshana principle, Nimbaditya-lila and the Acharya's divine mission.
body:
॥ Śrī Rādhā-Sarveśvaro Vijayate ॥

# The Divine Appearance and Sacred Life of Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan

Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan is the revered Acharya of the Nimbarka Sampradaya, an ardent worshipper of Shri Radha-Krishna Yugala, and the divine manifestation of Shri Sudarshana Chakraraja. His sacred life is not merely the biography of a great teacher; it is the glorious account of divine will, the unbroken guru lineage, the establishment of dharma, the protection of devotees and the worshipful service of Shri Radha-Sarveshvara.

## The Guru Lineage Beginning with Lord Hamsa

The divine guru lineage of the Nimbarka Sampradaya flows from Lord Hari in His Hamsa manifestation. At the beginning of creation, the four Kumaras—Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatana and Sanatkumara—sought the highest spiritual knowledge. Lord Hamsa appeared in response to their inquiry and instructed them in the knowledge of the Self and the yoga of Bhagavan. The sacred current of this instruction was transmitted by the Kumaras to Devarshi Narada. Thus Lord Hamsa, the four Kumaras and Devarshi Narada are the luminous foundations of this guru lineage.

## Initiation from Devarshi Narada

Devarshi Narada is the great teacher of Vaishnava devotion and divine wisdom. In the sacred account of Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan, the meeting with Narada, reverence to him and initiation received from him are central events. For the welfare of the world and the preservation of Vedic discipline, Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan appeared in the role of an Acharya and accepted Devarshi Narada as Guru. This divine conduct establishes the highest ideal of reverence for the Guru and the sacred discipline of discipleship.

Shri Nimbarkacharya's *Vedanta-Parijata-Saurabha* on Brahma Sutra 1.3.8 refers to the instruction given by the revered Kumaras to their Guru, Shri Narada. Purushottamacharya's explanation of the sixth verse of the *Dashashloki* explains 'Shri Naradaya' as 'to our Guru'. In the invocation of the *Vedanta-Kaustubha*, Shri Srinivasa Acharya offers reverence to Hamsa, the Kumaras, Devarshi Narada and Nimbabhaskara. The lineage is thus remembered with reverence in the Acharya literature.

## Shri Nimbarka as the Divine Principle of Sudarshana

Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan is the divine manifestation of Shri Sudarshana Chakraraja. Sudarshana is not merely the weapon of Bhagavan; He is the divine power of protection, illumination, destruction of ignorance and preservation of dharma. The sacred account describes the manifestation of this divine principle from the very beginning of creation, its radiant presence in the divine realms and its protection of sages and devotees.

## Protection of the Sages at Naimisharanya

When the austerities and sacrificial rites of the sages at Naimisharanya were disturbed by demonic forces, the divine Chakraraja manifested and destroyed those forces. The same divine principle appeared as Havirdhana and protected the sacrificial tradition. The sages praised the Lord, who assumed a gentle sage-like form and sanctified the sacred region by His presence.

## The Acharya's Mission and Digvijaya

For the welfare of the world, Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan appeared on earth as an Acharya, received initiation from Devarshi Narada and set forth to establish dharma, Vedic discipline, Vaishnava conduct and devotion to Bhagavan. His digvijaya was a divine journey to spread the light of dharma and bhakti throughout the world.

During this journey, the splendour of the divine incarnations shines through His deeds. The destruction of evil recalls Parashurama; the rescue of a boat and its passengers recalls Kurma; the deliverance of beings recalls Varaha; the protection of devotees recalls Narasimha; and the establishment of dharma recalls the sacred deeds of Shri Rama and Shri Balarama. The narrative also recalls the manifestations of Matsya, Vamana, Prithu and Kalki.

## The Purification of the Blood-Red River

During His journey, Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan met Sage Agastya. Learning of the sage's distress, He came to know of a river whose waters had turned blood-red through the curse of the sages of Dandakaranya. The Lord touched the river with His sacred feet, whereupon its waters became pure and holy. Sage Agastya then received the divine vision of the Chaturvyuha, adorned with conch, mace and lotus. The episode reveals the Acharya's compassion and His power to sanctify the sacred places.

## The Divine Fire Episode at Padmanabhapuri

At Padmanabhapuri, Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan blessed the virtuous and subdued hostile forces. While He was seated in solitude in a forest, wicked men surrounded Him and set fire around Him. Shri Padmanabha appeared in a fierce form. Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan prayed to the Lord for the protection of the Brahmins and all those who were afraid. The Lord's anger subsided, the fire was extinguished and all received fearlessness. The ocean itself offered worship to the Lord at the seashore. This is a radiant account of refuge and divine grace.

## Establishment of the Tapta-Mudra Tradition at Dvaraka

Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan reached Dvaraka and established the sacred Vaishnava observance of tapta-mudra. In the city of Shri Krishna, this rite affirmed the discipline of Vaishnava life and the sacred marks of devotion. The account also presents the Acharya's exposition of divine incarnations and the resolution of doctrinal questions.

## The Deliverance of the People at the Jain Festival

On the occasion of a Jain festival, Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan arrived at the gathering. A sacred stream emerged from the nail of His divine foot, and those present were caught in the waters and called out for refuge. The Lord saved them and led them to the path of Vaishnava devotion. The purpose of the Acharya's victory is the deliverance of souls and their establishment in devotion to Bhagavan.

## Return to Braja and Austerities at Nimbagrama

Having sanctified the world, Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan returned to Braja. At Nimbagrama, He remained absorbed in austerity and in the service of the lotus feet of Shri Narada Bhagavan. Though He had completed a divine mission across the world, His inner being remained immersed in the secret vision of Hari and loving service.

## The Debate with Vidyanidhi and the Vision of the Universal Form

At that time, the great scholar Vidyanidhi arrived. Having achieved victories in debate, he approached Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan with questions about His divine nature and doctrine. The Acharya answered according to the wisdom of His guru lineage, recalling the instruction of Lord Hamsa and the Kumaras.

During the debate, the Acharya held the setting sun in place so that the deliberation could reach its completion. Vidyanidhi was overwhelmed by the Lord's glory and sought refuge in Him. Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan then revealed the universal form, in which all the principles of creation—mind, senses, vital airs, subtle elements, gross elements, rivers, mountains, trees, rain, fire, tastes, fragrances and all moving and unmoving beings—were seen within the divine body. Vidyanidhi's learning blossomed into devotion, and he sought initiation and was accepted among the Lord's disciples.

## The Divine Nimbaditya-Lila

The sacred account also describes Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan's appearance in the world in the family of devoted Brahmins. The traditional narrative attributed to Shri Audumbar Rishi describes His appearance as Shri Sudarshana, known as Nimbaditya, on Vaishakha Shukla Tritiya at Nimbagrama near Govardhana, as the son of Jagannatha and Jayanti. The account also celebrates His fulfilment of the sacred duty towards His parents.

One day, when an ascetic guest arrived after the time for the meal had passed, Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan caused the light of the sun to shine upon a neem tree. Seeing the sunlight, the guest understood that the sun had not yet set and accepted the meal. The divine radiance upon the neem tree became the celebrated sign associated with the name Nimbarka or Nimbaditya. This lila shines as an example of hospitality, compassion and divine power.

## The Eternal Message of Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan

The sacred life of Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan proclaims devotion to the Guru, refuge in Bhagavan, Vaishnava conduct, surrender and loving worship of Shri Radha-Krishna Yugala. The lineage flowing from Lord Hamsa to the Kumaras, from the Kumaras to Narada, and from Narada to Shri Nimbarka Bhagavan is the unbroken stream of divine wisdom. The life of the Acharya itself is a scripture, illuminating the path of devotion, service and divine attainment.

॥ Śrī Rādhā-Sarveśvaro Vijayate ॥

**Author — Amit Sharma**
